title: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
subtitle: Transitions · 27 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **27 of the official questions in Transitions are this one** — 5 Easy, 15 Medium, 7 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- Sentence two points the same way as sentence one.
- Either it's a second, separate item of the same kind (another achievement, another use, another function), or it's the same claim restated more strongly or backed up with vivid support.
- Choices include 'additionally', 'in addition', 'moreover' or 'indeed' next to contrast and cause decoys.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Check that sentence two agrees with sentence one and doesn't turn against it.
- 2) If it's a new, parallel item, pick an addition word: additionally, in addition, moreover.
- If it strengthens, confirms or vividly elaborates the same point, pick 'indeed' or 'in fact'.
- 3) Make sure it isn't narrower (that would be example or specification) and isn't caused by sentence one.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: 'Indeed' feels wrong to you when sentence two seems to contrast with the words just before it.
In fact it supports the larger claim, for example by showing why something counts as an outlier.
You grab 'nevertheless' because of a surface contrast and miss that sentence two confirms the main point.
You also confuse 'moreover', which adds a new point, with 'indeed', which reinforces the same one.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
'Indeed' feels wrong to you when sentence two seems to contrast with the words just before it.
In fact it supports the larger claim, for example by showing why something counts as an outlier.
